q: Why is my nose so runny when I'm sick?
variants: how come i have so much snot when im sick
why do i keep needing tissues when i have a cold
why do i need so many tissues when im sick
a1: Your nose makes extra snot to wash the cold germs out.
a2: The germs make the inside of your nose puffy and wet. It stops when you get better.
ask_back: Do you think blowing your nose helps push the germs out?
notes: gap v3: cold (illness) vs feeling cold

q: Why are there so many stars in the sky?
variants: how come there are tons of stars
why is space full of stars
how come i can see so many stars on a dark night
a1: Space is so big, it holds more stars than anyone can count.
a2: New stars keep being made in huge clouds of gas and dust.
ask_back: Do you think you could ever count all the stars?

q: Are new stars still being made?
variants: are stars still being born
can a new star start shining
a1: Yes! New stars are still being made in space today.
a2: Gas and dust squeeze together into a ball. It gets so hot that it starts to shine.
ask_back: Do you think a new star starts big or small?

q: How do planets get their moons?
variants: where do moons come from
why do lots of planets have moons
how did the moons get around the planets
how does a planet get a moon
a1: Some planets caught rocks flying past. Others made moons from leftover bits.
a2: Our moon was probably made when a huge rock hit Earth.
ask_back: Do you think a big planet or a small planet holds more moons?

q: How many moons does Jupiter have?
variants: does jupiter have lots of moons
how many moons are around jupiter
does jupiter have a moon
a1: Jupiter has nearly a hundred moons that we know of.
a2: Four of them are big. Scientists keep finding more tiny ones.
ask_back: Can you guess how many moons our Earth has?
notes: gap v3 nearby (planets have moons); count changes as moons are found

q: Why does a comet have a tail?
variants: why do comets have long tails
how does a comet get its tail
why is there a glowing tail behind the comet
a1: Near the sun, a comet's ice warms up and turns into gas. Gas and dust stream out into a glowing tail.
a2: The sun pushes the tail, so it points away from the sun.
ask_back: Do you think the tail points toward the sun or away from it?

q: Why do comets come back?
variants: do comets come back again
how come a comet comes back after years
will the comet come back
why do we see the same comet again
a1: Comets go around the sun in long, stretched loops. So they come back near us again and again.
a2: Halley's Comet comes back about every 76 years.
ask_back: Can you guess how old you will be when Halley's Comet comes back?

q: Why does hail come in thunderstorms?
variants: why do storms make hail
how does hail get made in a storm
why do we get ice balls in a storm
why is there hail with thunder
a1: Big storm clouds have strong winds that blow raindrops up high. Up there, it is so cold the drops freeze.
a2: The ice balls grow until they are too heavy, then they fall.
ask_back: Do you think hail falls from small clouds or giant storm clouds?

q: Why do roots grow down into the ground?
variants: why roots go down
why dont roots grow up
why do plant roots go deep in the dirt
a1: Roots can feel the pull of the Earth, so they grow down.
a2: Down in the dirt, they find water and hold the plant tight.
ask_back: Do you think a root grows toward water or away from it?

q: Why do roots have tiny hairs?
variants: why are roots hairy
what are the little hairs on roots
why do roots look fuzzy
root hairs why
a1: Tiny root hairs soak up water from the soil.
a2: Lots of little hairs touch more dirt, so the plant drinks more.
ask_back: Can you guess if a plant drinks with its roots or its leaves?

q: Why are fruits so many different colours?
variants: why are some fruits red and some yellow
why is fruit so colorful
why arent all fruits the same color
a1: Bright colours help animals spot fruit when it is ripe.
a2: Animals eat it and drop the seeds far away. New plants grow there.
ask_back: Can you name a red fruit and a yellow fruit?

q: Why is bamboo so tall?
variants: how does bamboo get so tall
why do bamboo stalks grow so high
how come bamboo is taller than a house
why is bamboo really tall
a1: Bamboo is a giant grass that grows tall to reach the sun.
a2: Strong rings along the stem stop it from bending over.
ask_back: Do you think bamboo is a kind of tree or a kind of grass?

q: Why is bamboo hollow?
variants: why is bamboo empty inside
why does bamboo have a hole in the middle
how come bamboo is like a tube
bamboo hollow why
a1: A tube is strong but light, so bamboo can grow tall fast.
a2: Walls across the stem at each ring make it even stronger.
ask_back: Can you guess what people make from hollow bamboo?

q: How does a zipper stay closed?
variants: why does a zipper stay shut
how do zipper teeth stick together
why doesnt my zipper fall open
what makes a zip hold
a1: Each little tooth has a bump that fits into the next tooth.
a2: The pull pushes the teeth together, or pulls them apart.
ask_back: Can you look closely and find the little bumps on the teeth?

q: Why does a clock go tick tock?
variants: what makes the tick tock sound in a clock
why do clocks make a ticking noise
why does the clock click every second
where does the tick come from in a clock
a1: A small part inside lets the wheels turn in tiny steps. Each step makes a tick.
a2: Those even steps keep the hands moving at the right speed.
ask_back: Can you count the ticks for one minute?

q: Why don't some clocks tick?
variants: why is my clock quiet
why do some clocks not make a sound
how come the phone clock doesnt tick
why is there no tick in some clocks
a1: Some clocks move their hands smoothly, and some just show numbers. So they make no tick.
a2: Quiet clocks are nice in bedrooms.
ask_back: Can you find a clock that ticks, or one that is quiet?

q: How did the ocean get so deep?
variants: why is the bottom of the ocean so far down
how come the sea goes down so far
why is the sea deeper than a pool
a1: The sea floor sits much lower than the land. Water fills it up.
a2: The rock under the sea is heavy, so it sits low.
ask_back: Do you think the sea is deeper than a mountain is tall?

q: How deep is the ocean?
variants: how far down does the sea go
a1: In most places, the sea is about two miles deep.
a2: In one spot, it is deep enough to cover the tallest mountain.
ask_back: Do you think sunlight reaches all the way to the bottom?

q: Why do grown-ups vote?
variants: whats the point of voting
why do people go to vote
what is the point of a vote
a1: It lets everyone have a say when people must pick one thing.
a2: The pick with the most votes wins. That is fair.
ask_back: Do you think a class should vote on a game, or one kid picks?

q: How do you count votes?
variants: how do they count the votes
how do you know who won the vote
who counts all the votes
how does a vote get counted
a1: Each person gets one vote. Then people count the votes for each choice.
a2: The choice with the most votes wins.
ask_back: Can you guess what happens if two choices get the same number?

q: What is an election?
variants: whats an election
why do we have elections
what happens in an election
election what is it
a1: An election is a big vote to pick leaders.
a2: Grown-ups pick the people who will make the rules.
ask_back: Can you guess how old you have to be to vote?

q: Why do clouds look pink at sunset?
variants: how come the clouds go pink when the sun goes down
why are the clouds pink in the evening
why are the clouds all pink and orange tonight
a1: When the sun is low, its light looks pink and orange. Clouds catch that light and glow pink.
a2: That is why pink clouds show up at sunrise and sunset.
ask_back: Do you think pink clouds come in the morning, the evening, or both?

q: Why are some berries poisonous?
variants: how come some berries are bad to eat
why cant i eat the berries in the park
why can berries make your tummy hurt
a1: Some plants put poison in their berries so animals leave them alone.
a2: Many still look yummy. Never eat a wild berry without a grown-up.
ask_back: Should you eat a berry you find, or ask a grown-up first?

q: How can I tell which berries are safe to eat?
variants: how do i know if a berry is safe
which berries can i eat
can i eat berries from a bush
how do you know a berry is poisonous
a1: Safe and bad berries can look the same. You cannot tell by looking.
a2: Only eat berries a grown-up says are safe.
ask_back: Is it better to guess, or to ask a grown-up first?

q: Why can birds eat berries that make people sick?
variants: how come birds can eat poison berries
why dont bad berries hurt birds
why do birds eat berries we cant eat
can birds eat poisonous berries
a1: Birds' bodies can handle some berry poisons that make people sick.
a2: Birds drop the seeds far away, and that helps the plant spread.
ask_back: Does that mean berries birds eat are safe for us?

q: How did Jupiter get so big?
variants: why is jupiter the biggest planet
why is jupiter bigger than earth
what made jupiter grow so huge
a1: Jupiter formed far from the sun, where there was lots of gas. It grabbed huge amounts of it.
a2: That is why it is mostly gas, with no hard ground.
ask_back: Can you guess how many Earths could fit inside Jupiter?

q: What is Jupiter made of?
variants: is jupiter made of gas
what is inside jupiter
is jupiter rock or gas
a1: Jupiter is mostly made of gas, with no ground to stand on.
a2: Deep down, the gas gets squeezed so hard it turns runny.
ask_back: Do you think a spaceship could land on Jupiter?

q: Why do we draw stars with points?
variants: why is a star shape pointy
why do we draw a star with five points
why do star stickers have points
a1: Real stars are round, but they look sparkly and spiky. Points are an easy way to draw the sparkle.
a2: Five points is just a shape people like and can draw fast.
ask_back: Can you draw a star with five points without lifting your pencil?

q: Why do astronauts eat out of bags?
variants: why is space food in bags
why do astronauts keep food in pouches
why cant astronauts eat off a plate
how come astronaut food comes in packets
a1: In space, food floats. Bags keep crumbs and drops from floating away.
a2: Floating crumbs could get into eyes or machines.
ask_back: Can you guess what a drop of juice does in space?

q: How do astronauts drink in space?
variants: how do astronauts drink water
can astronauts drink from a cup
how do you drink juice in space
what do astronauts drink from
a1: Astronauts drink from pouches with a straw that closes.
a2: Water would float out of a cup in wobbly balls.
ask_back: Do you think water stays in a cup in space, or floats out?

q: How does the moon pull on the sea?
variants: why does the moon pull the ocean
how can the moon move the water
why does the sea follow the moon
does the moon really pull on the sea
a1: Big things pull on everything near them, and the moon is big. Sea water can move, so it slides toward the moon.
a2: That pull makes the tides. The sea comes in and goes out.
ask_back: Do you think the moon pulls on a puddle too, or only the sea?

q: Why are there two high tides a day?
variants: why does the sea come in twice a day
why are there two tides every day
how come the tide comes in two times
why does the tide go out and come back twice
a1: The moon pulls the sea into two bumps, one on each side.
a2: As Earth spins, most beaches pass through both bumps each day.
ask_back: Can you guess how many times a day the sea comes in?
notes: gap v3 nearby (tides); some places have one tide a day

q: Why is the vacuum cleaner so loud?
variants: how come the hoover makes a big noise
why does the vacuum roar
why does the vacuum hurt my ears
a1: A motor spins a fan super fast. The rushing air makes a loud roar.
a2: A stronger fan pulls up more dirt, but it is noisier too.
ask_back: Do you think a bigger fan makes more noise or less?

q: Why does a hair dryer make so much noise?
variants: why is the hair dryer loud
why does the hairdryer whirr
how come the blow dryer is noisy
hair dryer noise why
a1: A tiny fan inside spins very fast to blow air. The motor and rushing air make the whirring noise.
a2: The air also rushes past a hot wire to warm it up.
ask_back: Do you think the high setting is louder or quieter?

q: Why is the floor so cold in the morning?
variants: why is the floor freezing when i get up
how come the floor is cold when i wake up
why are my feet cold on the floor in the morning
why is the floor chilly in the morning
a1: The house cools down at night, and cool air sinks low.
a2: Your feet lose warmth into the cold floor, too.
ask_back: Do you think socks keep your feet warm on the floor?

q: How does an oven heat up?
variants: how does the oven make heat
what is the hot part inside the oven
how does the oven warm up
a1: Inside, metal bars get very hot when power runs through them. Some ovens burn gas instead.
a2: The walls keep the heat in, so the whole box gets hot.
ask_back: Can you guess why we wait before putting the cake in?

q: Why does the oven have a light inside?
variants: why is there a light in the oven
what is the oven light for
why does the oven light turn on
why do ovens have a lamp
a1: The light lets you see the food without opening the door.
a2: Opening the door lets hot air out, so baking takes longer.
ask_back: Can you guess why bakers peek through the glass?

q: How does a key open a lock?
variants: how does a key unlock a door
what does the key do inside the lock
why do keys have bumps
how does turning the key open the door
a1: Inside a lock are little pins that stop it from turning. The bumps on the right key push each pin just right.
a2: Then the lock can turn and open.
ask_back: Can you look at a key and count its bumps?

q: Why do my crayons break so easily?
variants: why do crayons snap
how come my crayon broke in half
why does my crayon break when i press hard
a1: Crayons are thin wax sticks, and they snap if you press hard.
a2: Dropping them can break them too.
ask_back: Do you think a short crayon or a long crayon breaks more easily?

q: Why does my crayon get flat at the tip?
variants: why does my crayon go blunt
why is my crayon not pointy anymore
where does the crayon go when i color
why do crayons get shorter
a1: Each time you color, a little bit rubs off on the paper.
a2: That wears the tip down and makes it flat.
ask_back: Can you turn your crayon to find a sharp edge again?

q: Why is there a flag on top of that building?
variants: why do buildings have flags
why do people hang flags outside
why do some houses have flags
a1: A flag shows which country or town a building is part of.
a2: People also hang flags to celebrate special days.
ask_back: Can you spot a flag on a building next time you are out?

q: Why do some flags have stars on them?
variants: why are there stars on flags
what do the stars on a flag mean
why does the american flag have stars
a1: Stars on a flag stand for something, like states.
a2: The flag of the USA has 50 stars, one for each state.
ask_back: Can you count the stars on a flag you know?

q: Why do people write letters to each other?
variants: why send a letter when you can call
why do we post letters
why do people mail cards and letters
a1: Letters let you send words to someone far away.
a2: A letter is something you can hold and keep. That makes it special.
ask_back: Do you think a letter or a phone call is more fun to get?
notes: gap v3 (mail letters vs alphabet letters)

q: How does a letter get to the right house?
variants: why do letters need an address
how does the mail know where to go
how does my letter find the right house
how does the post get to my house
a1: The address on the letter says where it must go.
a2: Letters get sorted by town, then street, then house.
ask_back: Can you guess what the numbers on houses are for?

q: Why does a flat stone skip on water?
variants: how do you make a stone skip
why does a rock bounce on the lake
how come a flat stone hops across the water
why do skipping stones bounce
a1: A flat stone thrown fast and low pushes down on the water. The water pushes back and bounces it up.
a2: It skips until it slows down, then it sinks.
ask_back: Do you think a round stone or a flat stone skips better?

q: How many times can a stone skip?
variants: whats the most skips ever
how many skips can a rock do
what is the record for skipping stones
a1: A good throw skips a few times. The world record is 88 skips!
a2: A flat stone, a fast throw and calm water help.
ask_back: Can you guess how many skips you could make?

q: Why does a rocket make a big cloud when it takes off?
variants: why is there so much smoke when a rocket launches
what is the big cloud under a rocket
why is a rocket launch so cloudy
a1: Much of the giant white cloud is steam. Water is sprayed under the rocket to protect the ground.
a2: The hot fire turns that water into a huge puffy cloud.
ask_back: Do you think the cloud is mostly smoke or mostly steam?

q: Why do cats love chasing string?
variants: why do cats play with string
why does my cat go crazy for a string
how come cats like yarn
why do cats chase a wiggly string
a1: A wiggly string moves like a mouse's tail. Cats chase it to practise hunting.
a2: Put the string away after play, so the cat can't swallow it.
ask_back: Do you think a cat likes a still string or a wiggly one?

q: Why do cats chase a laser dot?
variants: why do cats chase the red dot
why does my cat chase the light
how come cats go after a laser pointer
why do cats like lasers
a1: The quick little dot moves like a bug. Cats want to catch it.
a2: Never shine it in eyes. End with a real toy the cat can catch.
ask_back: Can you guess why the cat never catches the dot?
